crm_notes:
SUMMARY: Spectron is evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for productionizing an internal search + chat assistant for customer-facing trading support. Primary concern is latency tail and measurement alignment across teams (client, backend, infra). They will run a 4-week POC with reserved GPUs and want clear SLOs before procurement.

MEASUREMENT / SLO ALIGNMENT POINTS (customer language + our notes):
- They care about p50/p95/p99 but define them differently across teams. Product wants p95 <= 120ms for non-streaming 512-token requests; SRE says server-side p95 must be <= 80ms (they measure only server processing time). Need single source-of-truth.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: UX team measures first-byte latency for streaming (first token RTT) and end-to-stream for completion. Backend measures total tokens emitted. We recommended separate SLOs: streaming first-byte p50/p95, and completion-time p95 for short responses.
- Client-side timing: their browser-based client adds variable network + queue time. Action: instrument distributed tracing (client -> LB -> gateway -> runtime) and capture client-side spans. Agree to compare client-side p95 to server-side p95 with a documented offset budget.
- Percentile definitions: agree to compute percentiles on a rolling 1-hour window for alerting, aggregate daily for SLA reports. Use open-source hdr histogram implementation for consistent percentiles across infra.
- Token vs request timing: For streaming workloads, break out metrics: initial response latency (first byte), per-token emission rate, and completion latency. POC will record these as separate metrics.
- Batching & queueing effects: SRE stressed that batching improves throughput but can increase tail. We captured target regimes: low-latency mode (no batching, reserved capacity warmed) vs high-throughput mode (batching enabled, higher p95 allowed).

POC SUCCESS CRITERIA (agreed):
- Non-streaming: client-observed p95 <= 120ms on 512-token synthetic workload, p99 <= 300ms during business-hour 99th percentile load spikes.
- Streaming: first-byte p95 <= 60ms, per-token 95th latency <= 15ms on sustained 200 QPS with 64-token avg.
- Throughput: sustained tail-controlled throughput of 350 RPS at 1k concurrent connections on reserved 8x A100-like pool (approx). Redwood to provide capacity estimator runbook.
- Instrumentation: distributed traces from client through runtime, token-level metrics available in Console for POC window.
- Observability: cost/latency breakdown per-route in Console and alerting hooks for p95/p99 breaches.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR POC:
- Test harness: use reproducible synthetic workload (request sizes, prompt templates, and concurrency profiles). Run soak tests for 6h/day during the 4-week window.
- Percentile calculation: use HDR hist with 3-digit precision. Alerts fire on 5-min rollups of p95 > threshold for >3 consecutive windows.
- Clock sync: ensure client and server clocks NTP'ed; annotate traces with server_received_at and server_sent_first_token to compute server processing and network delta.
- Warm cache plan: pre-warm KV cache for heavy prompts; measure cold vs warm latencies and include cold-start budget in SLA (e.g., 95% exclude first 60s of backfill operations).
- Quantization & model variant routing: they requested a fallback variant for capacity constraints — Redwood to propose quantized 8-bit variant and expected latency uplift.

QUOTES / CUSTOMER COLOR: "We need to avoid surprises in day-1 — if the p99 slips during market opens we lose customers." — head of product.
